title: When the lamp’s oil runs out
odia:
ଦୀପରୁ ମାଲପା ସଇଲା
ପ୍ରଭୁଙ୍କ ଲୀଳା ଶେଷ ହେଲା।
literal_meaning: The oil in the lamp ran out; the Lord’s play came to an end.
meaning_odia: ଦୀପରୁ ତେଲ ସରିଯିବା ସହ ପ୍ରଭୁଙ୍କ ଲୀଳା ଶେଷ ହେବାକୁ ଏହି ଦୁଇ ଧାଡ଼ି ଯୋଡ଼ିଛି। ଯେଉଁ ସାଧନ ଉପରେ କୌଣସି କାମ ନିର୍ଭର କରେ, ସେହି ସାଧନ ସରିଲେ କାମ ମଧ୍ୟ ଅଟକିଯାଏ—ଏହା ଆମର ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠ। ମାଲପାର ଅର୍ଥ ତେଲ; ମୂଳ ବନାନ ବଦଳାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
explanation: The first line names a small material supply; the second announces an ending in the larger language of divine play. Our editorial reading notices dependence: an activity comes to a halt when what sustains it runs out. The verse itself leaves the particular occasion unspecified.
usage_example: Original imagined example: An ambitious programme stops as soon as its supplies are exhausted. Someone recalls the lamp whose oil ran out and brought the play to an end.
cultural_context: The pairing of lamp oil with the Lord’s play gives the ending its force. A modest material limit stands beside a grand expression of activity, making dependence on support visible.

witnesses.locator: Page25, second item beginning ଦୀପରୁ ମାଲପା.

english_summary: An activity ends when its supporting resources run out.
